key_insight: FREDI combines proportional-fair wireless resource allocation with dual-threshold early-exit inference to securely offload only critical events from UEs to edge servers, aiming for near-optimal utility and fairness.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical optimization recipe for secure edge AI systems that must balance latency, compute, bandwidth, and user fairness at scale.
method: Early-exit CNN screening on each UE using two confidence thresholds to decide local vs. edge inference
Joint optimization of UE–ES association, bandwidth, transmit power, processing, and thresholds under proportional-fair utility
Exact threshold search over the finite empirical confidence set plus mixed-integer exponential-cone resource allocation with certified optimality gap
evidence_signal: Experiments with early-exit MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 report near-perfect UE fairness, aggregate utility close to a Sum-Utility benchmark, and Stage-A scaling from 6 to 144 UEs with median solve time below 0.1 s.
watch_item: The certified optimization relies on precise confidence statistics and an exponential-cone/MIP solver pipeline, so performance and scalability may depend on model calibration and solver availability.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
